view.stem: In the radio receiver shown, the tuning coil has inductance $L=2\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{H}$, and the variable capacitor's capacitance $C$ can vary continuously from $12$ to $450\,\mathrm{pF}$, including both endpoints. Use the ideal LC resonance model, neglecting parasitic capacitance and the detector section's effect on tuning, and take the electromagnetic-wave speed as $c=3.0\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}$. Which option correctly gives the complete tunable wavelength range and the capacitances corresponding to the shortest and longest wavelengths? Round wavelengths to one decimal place.

options.text: The wavelength range is approximately $14.7$ to $90.0\,\mathrm{m}$; the shortest wavelength corresponds to $C=12\,\mathrm{pF}$, and the longest to $C=450\,\mathrm{pF}$.

intent.task: Determine the full tuning-wavelength interval of an ideal LC receiver with fixed inductance and variable capacitance, convert pF to F, and assign the two capacitance endpoints to the shortest and longest wavelengths. The task is not one wavelength at an arbitrary capacitance or a sequence of numerical blanks.
intent.source_solution: Solved independently before alternatives: an ideal LC circuit obeys Lq''+q/C=0, giving angular frequency omega_0=1/sqrt(LC) and ordinary frequency f_0=1/(2 pi sqrt(LC)). Resonant tuning requires the incident frequency to equal f_0, so lambda=c/f_0=2 pi c sqrt(LC). Convert 12 pF to 1.2e-11 F and 450 pF to 4.5e-10 F. With L=2e-4 H and c=3e8 m/s, the endpoint wavelengths are 12 pi sqrt(6) m=92.34358777165421 m and 180 pi m=565.4866776461628 m. Since lambda increases continuously and strictly with positive C, the full closed interval is [12 pi sqrt(6),180 pi] m, approximately 92.3 to 565.5 m; 12 pF gives the shortest wavelength and 450 pF the longest. The brackets include the exact attainable endpoints; displayed decimals are rounded. Necessary conditions are that the given C is the effective tuning capacitance, L is fixed, loss/parasitic capacitance/detector loading are neglected, and the specified wave speed is used. The separate right-hand detector capacitor is not added to C. This is an ideal tuning range, not a guarantee of sufficiently strong broadcasts at every wavelength.
intent.unit_reason: A complete wavelength interval together with its capacitance-endpoint mapping is one coherent tuning-range judgment, so one native single-choice item is appropriate. Each of the four alternatives is a complete individually testable result and exactly one is true. The endpoints are not split into arithmetic clicks, and the alternatives are not combination codes.
limitations: Selecting a complete correct result cannot establish unaided production of the LC formula, SI conversion and numerical working.
Endpoint correspondence is still tested, but selection cannot establish unaided written explanations of wavelength monotonicity and the resonance condition.

figure_observations.observation: Actually opened the specified original PNG and complete 640x400 modern SVG preview, for two images cumulatively. In both, the left coil and diagonally arrow-marked variable capacitor connect across the same tuning nodes, with antenna above and ground below. The modern L and C labels are readable. Beyond the diode are a separate detector/output capacitor and the far-right headphones. The full right edge, lower return, ground and Headphones label are visible. The right output capacitor is not the given variable C; no numerical wavelength or solution formula is printed. The two isolated repo SVG byte hashes both equal the seed hash 4f96fbe7ced0f00ff3651b240860b159141b018683297f806f9dc62886878529. Actual image opens and PNG hashes are recorded in opens.json.

rationales.derivation: Mistaking angular frequency 1/sqrt(LC) for ordinary frequency gives lambda_wrong=c sqrt(LC), omitting 2 pi. Substituting 12 pF and 450 pF yields 14.696938456699069 m and 90.00000000000001 m, which round to this alternative. The endpoint direction is increasing, but both wavelengths are wrong.
rationales.misconception: Treat omega_0 as f_0 and use lambda=c/omega_0 rather than lambda=2 pi c/omega_0, losing the factor 2 pi.

rationales.derivation: Calculate and sort the two wavelengths correctly as 92.3 m and 565.5 m, but label the endpoints using the frequency trend instead of the wavelength trend. Because f_0 decreases as C increases, forgetting lambda=c/f_0 leads to pairing larger C with the shortest wavelength and smaller C with the longest. The numerical range is right, but both capacitance-endpoint correspondences are reversed.
rationales.misconception: Keep correctly computed wavelength values, then confuse frequency with wavelength when assigning endpoints, treating the decreasing dependence of f_0 on C as the dependence of lambda on C.

rationales.derivation: Compute the 12 pF endpoint correctly as 92.34358777165421 m, then assume wavelength is proportional to C at fixed L. Multiply by 450/12=37.5 to get 3462.884541437033 m, rounding to 3462.9 m. The actual wavelength ratio is sqrt(450/12)=6.123724356957945, not 37.5.
rationales.misconception: Extrapolate from one correct endpoint using the capacitance ratio instead of its square root, replacing lambda proportional to sqrt(C) with lambda proportional to C.

rationales.derivation: Use lambda=2 pi c sqrt(LC) with 12 pF=1.2e-11 F and 450 pF=4.5e-10 F to obtain 92.34358777165421 m and 565.4866776461628 m. Since lambda increases continuously and strictly for positive C, 12 pF gives the shortest wavelength and 450 pF the longest, with both endpoints attainable. Rounding as requested gives 92.3 m and 565.5 m.

omitted_tasks: Unaided written production of the LC formula, SI conversion and endpoint numerical working is not assessed.
Unaided written explanations of wavelength monotonicity and the resonance condition are not assessed.
coverage.reason: One item covers the only seed. It retains the original L, C interval, pF/H units, LC tuning model, complete wavelength range and both capacitance-endpoint correspondences. The ideal model, wave speed and attainable endpoint conditions are explicit without supplying the solution formula or correct range. No numerical endpoint or endpoint-reasoning task is dropped; the distinction between recognition and independent written calculation is recorded honestly without inventing an open-ended question.
